comment: One-line game briefs for scripts/bench/gameMakerBatch.mts. Each is one Game Maker turn. Ids are stable and land in the batch manifest, so a Laminar trace can be read back against the prompt that produced it. Keep briefs inside the skill's scope: one HTML canvas, plain JS, keyboard or pointer input, no extra libraries or assets beyond a generated cover.

briefs.brief: A dodger where you slide a ship left and right to avoid falling rocks, with a score that counts survived seconds.
A breakout clone: paddle, bouncing ball, a wall of bricks in rows of different colours, and three lives.
Snake on a grid: eat pellets to grow, die on your own tail or the wall, show the high score.
Pong against a simple computer opponent that tracks the ball a little imperfectly, first to 7 points wins.
A one-button flappy game: tap to flap through gaps in scrolling pipes, score one per pipe passed.
Asteroids: rotate and thrust a ship with wrap-around edges, shoot rocks that split into smaller ones.
A space shooter with a formation of aliens that step sideways and descend, and a player cannon at the bottom.
A single-screen platformer: run and jump across three ledges to reach a flag, with gravity and coyote-time jumping.
An endless upward jumper where the camera follows you as you bounce from platform to platform, falling off screen ends the run.
A tiny tower defence: enemies walk a fixed path, click to place turrets that shoot them, lose a life per leak.
A typing game where words fall from the top and you clear them by typing them correctly before they land.
A memory match game: a 4x4 grid of face-down cards, flip two at a time, timer and move counter.
Whack-a-mole with nine holes, moles that pop up for shrinking windows, and a 30 second timer.
A maze escape: a generated grid maze, arrow-key movement, a visible exit and a step counter.
A small Sokoban: push crates onto marked targets on a tile grid, with undo and a level reset key.
A falling-block puzzle with four piece shapes, rotation, line clears and increasing speed.
A match-three grid where you swap adjacent gems to clear lines of three or more, with cascading refills.
A lunar lander: burn fuel to touch down slowly on a flat pad over jagged terrain, crash if too fast.
A top-down lane racer: dodge traffic on a scrolling three-lane road, speed rises with distance.
A helicopter cave flyer: hold to rise, release to fall, thread a narrowing scrolling tunnel.
A bubble shooter: aim with the mouse and fire coloured bubbles at a hanging cluster, matches of three pop.
A basket catcher: catch falling fruit for points and dodge falling bombs, three misses and it is over.
A reaction test: circles appear at random spots and shrink, click before they vanish, report average reaction time.
A Simon-says game: four coloured pads flash a growing sequence you have to repeat by clicking.
Minesweeper on a 9x9 board: left click reveals with flood fill, right click flags, win by clearing all safe tiles.
Tic-tac-toe against an unbeatable computer player, with a win line drawn and a rematch button.
A shooting gallery: targets slide across three rows at different speeds, limited ammo, click to shoot.
A rhythm tapper: notes scroll down four lanes towards a hit line, score perfect, good or miss per key press.
An idle clicker: click a field to harvest coins, buy two upgrades that add income per second, numbers keep ticking.
A gravity puzzle: launch a probe with a drag of the mouse so it slingshots around a planet into a target ring.
A stacking game: blocks swing across the screen and you click to drop them, the tower narrows on bad drops.
Light cycles: two riders leave solid trails on a bounded arena, player against a simple computer rider.
